statement: The supplied source does not contain a derivation of the non-linear least squares normal equations from linearization (the derivation steps are omitted in the truncated source text). Non-linear least squares is defined as the form of least squares analysis used to fit a set of m observations with a model that is non-linear in n unknown parameters (m >= n) by approximating the model by a linear one and refining the parameters by successive iterations. The defining normal equations in matrix notation are (J^T J) Delta beta = J^T Delta y, or more generally for weighted least squares minimizing S = sum_{i=1}^m W_{ii} r_i^2, (J^T W J) Delta beta = J^T W Delta y.

symbols.meaning: vector of differences between observed data and calculated model values
Jacobian matrix of partial derivatives of model values with respect to parameters
diagonal weight matrix with elements ideally equal to reciprocal error variances
objective function (sum of squares or weighted sum of squares of residuals)
partitioned upper-trapezoidal matrix containing upper triangular block R_n and zero block
upper triangular n x n submatrix of R

properties.why: Parameters are updated iteratively via beta^{k+1} = beta^k + Delta beta where Delta beta solves the normal equations
The system expands in index notation to sum_{i=1}^m sum_{s=1}^n J_{ij} J_{is} Delta beta_s = sum_{i=1}^m J_{ij} Delta y_i for j = 1, ..., n
Minimizing the weighted sum of squares S = sum_{i=1}^m W_{ii} r_i^2 yields (J^T W J) Delta beta = J^T W Delta y
Decomposing J = Q R avoids forming normal equations and gives the shift vector by solving R_n Delta beta = (Q^T Delta y)_n
Modifying normal equations to (J^T W J + lambda I) Delta beta = (J^T W) Delta y rotates the shift vector toward the steepest descent vector J^T W Delta y when lambda I >> J^T W J
Updating beta^{k+1} = beta^k + f Delta beta reduces the step length while preserving direction to prevent divergence
The objective function is quadratic with respect to parameters with elliptical contours only in a region close to its minimum where truncated Taylor series holds

assumptions.assumption: The number of observations m is greater than or equal to the number of unknown parameters n (m >= n).
assumptions.breaks_when: There are fewer observations than parameters (m < n), making the parameter estimates undetermined.

assumptions.assumption: The initial parameter estimates are sufficiently close to optimal values that the objective function is approximately quadratic.
assumptions.breaks_when: Initial estimates deviate strongly from optimal values, causing objective contours to depart from elliptical shape and the Gauss-Newton algorithm to diverge.

assumptions.assumption: The normal equations matrix J^T J (or J^T W J) is positive definite.
assumptions.breaks_when: The parameter set is at or near a stationary point (e.g. saddle point or maximum between multiple minima) where the gradient vanishes and descent direction is undefined.

assumptions.assumption: For linearizing transformations (e.g., logarithmic transforms of exponential models), experimental errors are multiplicative and log-normally distributed.
assumptions.breaks_when: Errors are additive or not log-normal, causing the linearized objective to yield biased and inconsistent parameter estimates.

failure_modes.signature: Objective function S increases from one iteration to the next or parameter shifts grow excessively.
failure_modes.cause: Initial parameter estimates lie outside the local quadratic region, or shift vector direction is poor.

failure_modes.signature: Normal equations matrix J^T W J is not positive definite, leading to numerical failure in Cholesky decomposition or undefined search direction.
failure_modes.cause: Iterates approach a maximum, saddle point, or point of zero parameter scale (such as zero half-width in Lorentzian fitting) between multiple minima.

failure_modes.signature: Convergence criteria are satisfied, but the resulting sum of squares S is strictly greater than the global minimum value.
failure_modes.cause: The objective surface exhibits multiple minima due to non-linear model structure, parameter powers, or periodicity.

failure_modes.signature: Multiple parameter values yield identical optimal values of the objective function (e.g., sign ambiguity hat{beta} vs -hat{beta}, or periodic shift beta + 2n pi).
failure_modes.cause: Model contains parameters raised to even powers, symmetric products (alpha beta = beta alpha), or trigonometric functions.

failure_modes.signature: Estimated parameters and standard deviations differ from true values, or fits are heavily biased toward specific data ranges (e.g., Lineweaver-Burk plots).
failure_modes.cause: Applying linearizing transformations when errors are additive rather than multiplicative and log-normal.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so nonlinear_least_squares is recorded as a definition
